lead: Multiple pregnancy is more than one fetus in the uterus; twins occur naturally in about 1 in 80 (Hellin's law: triplets 1 in 80²). Chorionicity, not zygosity, decides the risk, and prematurity is the main cause of death.
f: Dizygotic (about two thirds): 2 ova + 2 sperm, either sex, always DCDA · Monozygotic (one third, constant): split day decides the type · Split by day 3: DCDA; days 4–8: MCDA (commonest MZ); days 8–13: MCMA; after day 13: conjoined · Risk factors (DZ): IVF, clomiphene, previous twins, family history, age and parity, African race

Severe hyperemesis, uterus large for dates, many fetal parts, two hearts · Ultrasound: number, viability; chorionicity at 11–13⁺⁶ wk; if late and unclear, treat as MC · Lambda (twin-peak) sign → DC; T sign → MC; two placentas or two sexes → DC; no membrane → MCMA · Large for dates: wrong dates, polyhydramnios, macrosomia, fibroids, ovarian mass, mole

sc: One placenta, thick membrane with a triangular wedge at 12 wk → Dichorionic (lambda sign)

f: Maternal: hyperemesis, anaemia, pre-eclampsia (about 5 times), GDM, preterm labour, polyhydramnios, praevia, APH, malpresentation, PPH, operative birth · Fetal: miscarriage, vanishing twin, anomalies (twice in MC), prematurity, FGR (25%), discordance, stillbirth, cerebral palsy · Labour: malpresentation, cord prolapse, hypoxia of twin 2, locked twins

TTTS (10–15% of MC): artery-to-vein links pump blood from donor to recipient; untreated mortality up to 80% · Donor: anaemic, oligohydramnios ('stuck twin'), FGR, small bladder · Recipient: polycythaemic, polyhydramnios, large bladder, heart failure, hydrops · Treatment: fetal medicine; fetoscopic laser under 26 wk · TAPS: Hb gap, liquor equal (MCA Doppler) · TRAP: acardiac twin fed by the pump twin · Discordance over 25% needs referral

sc: MCDA at 20 wk, deep pool 10 cm in one sac, other twin stuck → TTTS: fetoscopic laser

f: DC: early loss harmless (vanishing twin); later: preterm labour (90% deliver within 3 wk) · MC: the survivor bleeds into the dead twin; up to 25% die or have brain damage at that moment, so rushed delivery does not help · Weekly scans, check maternal clotting, aim for about 36 wk

sc: MC twins, one dies at 30 wk → Do not rush delivery

f: Team care, more visits · Iron and folic acid; CBC at booking and 28 wk · BP and urine every visit (moderate risk factor for PE) · Scans: chorionicity 11–13⁺⁶ wk, NT, anomaly scan · DC: growth scan every 4 wk from 20 wk · MC: every 2 wk from 16 wk (TTTS) · Steroids if preterm birth is likely; birth plan by 36 wk

DCDA 37 wk · MCDA 36 wk (NICE NG137; local practice often 38 and 37 wk) · MCMA 32 wk by CS (cord entanglement) · Triplets 35 wk by CS · Twin 1 cephalic: aim for vaginal birth, whatever twin 2 · CS if twin 1 is non-cephalic, MCMA, triplets or usual reasons

Hospital, IV line, group and save, continuous CTG of both, epidural ideal · After twin 1: hold twin 2 longitudinal; restart oxytocin if contractions fade; ARM once the head enters the pelvis · Twin 2 transverse with intact sac: ECV; with ruptured sac: internal podalic version · Third stage: active management + oxytocin infusion for 2–4 h (PPH)

sc: Twin 2 cephalic, membranes intact, contractions weak → Oxytocin, then ARM once the head enters the pelvis
tr: Locked twins: twin 1 breech and twin 2 cephalic; prevented by caesarean when twin 1 is breech
